title: Microalgae Classification Using Improved Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: Microalgae are present at all levels of nutrients and food networks, so in aquatic environments they are an important part of the food chain of aquatic organisms, which also play an important role as biological purifiers of water resources and regulation. They also affect the pH of the environment; also plants are the only organisms capable of synthesizing long-chain fatty acids. Therefore, microalgae are the supplier and primary source of unsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) for all organisms present in the food chain of the aquatic environment. It should be noted that many microalgae are also biological indicators of water and reflect the ecological status of the environment. Precise classification of microalgae is related to the human observation capability. The present study proposes a new optimized classification technique with higher accuracy to provide a computer-aided classification of the microalgae. The method begins with an image segmentation to determine the region of interest. The segmentation part has been optimized by a new metaheuristic to provide higher accuracy. Then, the features have been extracted and fed to a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for final classification. The comparison results of the proposed method with some other methods show that the proposed method with 0.828 Kappa, and 0.342 and 0.855 min and max value of F1, provides the highest accuracy compared to the others.

title: Optimizing SVM hyperparameters for satellite imagery classification using metaheuristic and statistical techniques
abstract: Abstract Hyperparameters tuning is an important process through which the hyperparameters of a machine learning model are selected. The hyperparameters tuning process involves searching for the optimal hyperparameters of a machine learning model that enhances its performance and accuracy. Unlike model parameters, which are learned through the training process, hyperparameters are predefined and guide the training process. Hyperparameter tuning has gained interest due to its impact on the model’s performance. In machine learning competitions, hyperparameter tuning is often the difference between a mid-tier model and a leaderboard-topping solution. In this paper, hyperparameters of support vector machine (SVM) are optimized through the use of metaheuristic and statistical approaches to classify satellite imagery. Metaheuristic approaches are inspired by natural phenomena, and they explore the search space of the hyperparameters to find the optimal or near-optimal parameters. Statistical approaches use probabilistic models to identify the hyperparameters that maximize the model’s performance. In this paper, four metaheuristic and four statistical approaches are used. The metaheuristic approaches used are particle swarm optimization, simulated annealing, genetic algorithm, and cuckoo Search. The statistical approaches used are Bayesian optimization, successive halving algorithm, tree-structured Parzen estimator optimization, and Metropolis–Hastings Markov chain Monte Carlo. Experiments are performed on a satellite imagery classification problem. Different metrics are used to assess the performance of each algorithm, namely, accuracy, f1 score, precision, recall, and run-time. Tree-structured Parzen estimator achieves the best results for all metrics among most of the experiments with reasonable run-times proving its robustness and its practical applicability to tune the hyperparameters of SVM.
